bug_semantics: The boards plugin's file endpoints authorize only board-level access (hasValidReadTokenForBoard / permissions.HasPermissionToBoard(boardID, PermissionViewBoard)) and then fetch the requested file by its raw server-side name with no check that the file actually belongs to that board: handleServeFile/getFileInfo call a.app.GetFileInfo(filename) and a.app.GetFileReader(teamID, boardID, filename) directly on the attacker-supplied filename. Because file names are opaque server-generated identifiers (e.g. 32-byte UUIDs/hashes stored under teamID/boardID paths), any authenticated user who can view ANY board can pass board-level authorization for their own board and then enumerate UUIDs of files belonging to other teams/boards, downloading sensitive attachments (CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key).
flaw_origin: Commit c1f2ae63165dfc5a162b6d364c3f1644e5114a1c ("Rest API reorganization (#3624)", 2022-08-10, author Doug Lauder) created server/api/files.go and moved the file-serving handler onto the teamID/boardID/filename route with the board-level-only authorization and unvalidated GetFileReader(board.TeamID, boardID, filename) call — the exact object-key/filename decoupling the advisory describes. The handler's board-scoped check with an unvalidated filename (GetFileInfo + GetFileReader by bare filename) is present verbatim in this commit's server/api/files.go; the vulnerable GET-file endpoint previously lived inside the monolithic server/api/api.go and was restructured by this commit. The getFileInfo sibling endpoint that leaks file metadata via the same unvalidated filename was added in 66744020794c9b451c5adb90164cd2c1945e542c (2022-11-24, "File attachment in the card (#4053)") with identical board-only authorization. The fix (3f3e3becfe1d66db0d0f4fd235f04afd6e1ec40b) adds ValidateFileOwnership() to both endpoints, confirming the missing per-file ownership validation as the vulnerable semantics.
